topic: AI-generated code; uncertainty estimation; software quality and security; human review triage
status: bounded research-design lead from three lexical-priority full texts in one 2020-2024 topic-period cell; not a prevalence estimate or novelty claim
claim: Existing evidence in this sample supports uncertainty as a potentially useful discriminator for some fully correct versus erroneous code-generation outputs, but does not establish calibrated, severity-aware review utility across code synthesis, repair, security, and code-change tasks. Partial test-passing errors, model/dataset/distance sensitivity, and text-overlap outcomes leave a concrete need to test whether uncertainty improves held-out review triage at a fixed human-review budget.
positive_evidence: Look Before You Leap evaluates seven code-capable LLMs on HumanEval and MBPP and reports that sample-based uncertainty generally ranks errors better than single-inference measures; performance differs across models/datasets and uncertainty distance functions.

That study identifies a key failure mode: 40.4% of GPT-3.5 MBPP errors pass at least one test, versus 27.3% for GPT-4o and 32.4% for GPT-4o mini. Its target is complete correctness, so these partial failures challenge a coarse correct/incorrect label for real risk triage.

Astraios evaluates code synthesis/repair with Pass@1, robustness under ReCode perturbations, and security across a bounded set of 40 automatically testable AATK scenarios; it reports model-scale effects and finds larger models less robust/secure in its tested settings, but does not combine these outcomes with uncertainty scores.

The code-change study shows that examples and PEFT can improve review generation, commit messages, and comment updates, but measures the generated text mainly with BLEU/B-Norm/GLEU or exact-comment accuracy; its limited human evaluation concerns commit-message quality, not defects caught or vulnerabilities avoided.
counterevidence: The uncertainty study reports above-chance risk discrimination for many tested code model/dataset pairs, so uncertainty is not useless; sample-based estimation often improves ranking.

Astraios employs execution-based Pass@1 and security scenarios, while the code-change study adds repository-derived data and some human review, demonstrating that direct outcome evaluation is feasible in parts of this space.
Different outcome types need not share a single uncertainty score: the observed variation may be expected task dependence rather than a defect in each task-specific method.
The papers use different models, datasets, and evaluation versions; this three-paper sample cannot show that uncertainty-based code triage has never been studied or establish a general failure rate.

sources.sections: Sections IV-B, V-C/V-D; Table V; partial-error and distance-function analysis
Sections 2.3 and results on HumanEvalPack, ReCode robustness, AATK security; conclusions
Sections 2.1 and 3.1-3.4; task metrics, PEFT/model results, category analysis and human evaluation

falsifiable_test: On project/time-held-out code synthesis, repair, and code-change tasks, collect model uncertainty before evaluation and compare it with execution tests, mutation tests, vulnerability tests, and blinded maintainer review. Stratify by model family/scale, perturbation, error severity, and comment-only versus executable-code changes. Report AUC, Brier score/reliability curves, selective risk at fixed review budgets, missed critical defects, and reviewer minutes per confirmed issue against pass@1, token confidence, and static-analysis baselines. The lead weakens if uncertainty fails to improve calibration or critical-defect yield at equal review cost; it strengthens if it does so robustly across held-out projects/task types. Not run in this audit.
limitations: Only three purposively retrieved records from one topic-period cell; not a random estimate of the whole corpus or of code-generation literature. The uncertainty study uses bounded benchmark subsets and complete correctness as its principal code outcome; the Astraios security analysis is restricted to automatically testable scenarios; code-change metrics mostly use textual references. No outputs were regenerated, no common codebase or model was rerun, and no novelty search was completed.
